hints.title: In-Place List Interleaving
hints.text: Interleaving nodes from the beginning and end requires access to the second half in reverse order. How can you split and reverse the second half in-place?

hints.title: Three Sub-problems Composition
hints.text: Locate the midpoint using unequal speed traversal, reverse the second half in-place, and alternate merging nodes from both halves.

hints.title: Split Reverse Interleave Procedure
hints.text: Find the list middle. Sever the connection after the middle node to create two separate lists. Reverse the second list in-place. Interleave nodes by alternately splicing one node from the first list and one from the reversed second list.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def reorderList(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> None:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return
        slow, fast = head, head
        while fast and fast.next:
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next
        prev, curr = None, slow.next
        slow.next = None
        while curr:
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
        first, second = head, prev
        while second:
            tmp1, tmp2 = first.next, second.next
            first.next = second
            second.next = tmp1
            first, second = tmp1, tmp2
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 5 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Three sequential linear passes (midpoint, reversal, interleaving) all in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Storing all nodes in an array takes O(N) space and fails the problem requirement of modifying nodes in-place without node allocation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Combining midpoint detection, list reversal, and list interleaving achieves O(N) time with O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Breaking the problem into 3 standard subroutines, severing the link between first and second half (prev.next = None), and clean pointer manipulation without cycles.
